pages.text: By day, an upper paddy overflowed. A rushing sound came from just one spot.
At night, Dingding lay down. That same rushing again! "I want quiet to sleep."
"Mom, that earlier sound—" "Rain. Go to sleep."
Dingding tried again. "No, outside the window—" "Yes, I know."
Dingding looked out. Not one raindrop. Stars everywhere.
Mom was already sleeping. Snore, snore.
Dingding shook Grandma awake. "Overflowing water." She lit a lantern.
Hand in hand, they climbed to the upper field. A broken bank poured water.
Dingding held the lamp tight. Grandma packed soil in. The rushing stopped. From home came only Mom's snores.
